questions.question: South Africa ended a 27-year wait for a major cricket title by winning which tournament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Test Championship**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **South Africa** secured a historic victory in the **World Test Championship**, effectively ending a **27-year** wait for a major **International Cricket Council (ICC)** trophy.
 
• The last time the South African national team, known as the **Proteas**, won a premier global cricket tournament was the **ICC KnockOut Trophy** (now known as the **Champions Trophy**) held in **1998**.
 
• The **World Test Championship** is a league competition for **Test cricket** run by the **ICC**, which began its first cycle in **2019** to determine the ultimate world champion in the longest format of the game.
 
• Winning this title is a significant milestone for South African cricket, as the team had previously reached multiple **semi-finals** in various formats but failed to cross the final hurdle until this **WTC** triumph.
 
• The victory signifies **South Africa's** dominance in the red-ball format over a **two-year** cycle, involving rigorous series against other top-ranked nations like **Australia**, **India**, and **England**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC Champions Trophy 1998:**
 
 
• The inaugural edition of the **ICC KnockOut Trophy** was held in **Bangladesh** in **October 1998**.
 
• **South Africa** emerged as the champions after defeating the **West Indies** in the final match in **Dhaka**, with **Hansie Cronje** leading the side.
 
 
 
• **World Test Championship (WTC) Format:**
 
 
• The **WTC** was introduced to bring more relevance to **Test cricket**. The competition features the **top nine** Test-playing nations.
 
• Points are awarded for each match, and the **two teams** with the highest percentage of points at the end of the cycle compete in a **one-off final** at a neutral venue, often in **England** at **Lord's** or **The Oval**.
 
 
 
• **South Africa's Cricket Legacy:**
 
 
• The country was banned from international cricket between **1970** and **1991** due to the **apartheid** policy.
 
• Since their return in **1991**, they have produced legendary players such as **Jacques Kallis**, **AB de Villiers**, **Dale Steyn**, and **Hashim Amla**.
 
• Despite their individual brilliance, the "chokers" tag haunted them for **decades** due to heartbreaking losses in the **1992**, **1999**, and **2015** **World Cup** knockouts.
 
 
 
• **Other ICC Tournaments:**
 
 
• The **ICC Cricket World Cup** (50-over format) and the **ICC T20 World Cup** are the other major trophies that **South Africa** has competed for over the years.
 
• Winning the **World Test Championship** is often considered the most prestigious achievement in modern cricket due to the endurance and skill required over **five-day** matches.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which international agency raised concerns leading to amendments in India’s anti-doping law in July 2025?

options.text: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** is the primary international body responsible for regulating and monitoring the fight against drugs in sports. In **July 2025**, India introduced critical amendments to its **National Anti-Doping Act** following concerns raised by **WADA** regarding compliance with the **World Anti-Doping Code**.
 
• The amendments aimed to ensure that India's legal framework for sports remains consistent with **international standards**, specifically addressing the independence of the **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** and the **National Anti-Doping Laboratory (NDTL)**.
 
• The **World Anti-Doping Code** is a document that harmonizes anti-doping policies, rules, and regulations within sport organizations and among public authorities around the world. Failure to comply with this code can lead to sanctions, including the suspension of a country's ability to host international sporting events. ***Hence, the statement regarding WADA raising concerns is correct.***
 
• In the context of the **2025** legislative update, the focus was on enhancing **data protection** for athletes and streamlining the **results management** process to prevent delays in adjudicating doping cases.
 
• The **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** of India, established in **2005**, is mandated to implement anti-doping programs in the country in accordance with **WADA** guidelines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA):**
 
 
• **WADA** was established on **November 10, 1999**, in **Lausanne, Switzerland**, following the **Declaration of Lausanne**. Its current headquarters are located in **Montreal, Canada**.
 
• It is a **foundation** initiated by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** to promote, coordinate, and monitor the fight against doping in sports in all its forms.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO’s Role:**
 
 
• The **United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)** adopted the **International Convention against Doping in Sport** in **2005**.
 
• This convention is the legal instrument through which governments formally commit to the **WADA Code**, as **WADA** is a private non-governmental organization.
 
 
 
• **International Olympic Committee (IOC):**
 
 
• While the **IOC** works closely with **WADA**, its primary function is the organization and governance of the **Olympic Games** and the promotion of **Olympism** worldwide.
 
• The **IOC** provides significant funding to **WADA**, but the agency operates as an independent international body.
 
 
 
• **National Anti-Doping Bill, 2022:**
 
 
• Before the **2025** amendments, India passed the **National Anti-Doping Bill in 2022**, which provided statutory backing to **NADA** and established the **National Board for Anti-Doping in Sports**.
 
• This legislative framework is essential for maintaining the **National Anti-Doping Laboratory (NDTL)**’s **WADA accreditation**, which is necessary for the international validity of test results.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Banned Substances:** **WADA** maintains an annual **Prohibited List**, which identifies substances and methods prohibited at all times, in-competition only, and in specific sports (e.g., **anabolic agents**, **peptide hormones**, and **masking agents**).
 
• **Whereabouts Requirements:** Athletes in a **Registered Testing Pool (RTP)** must provide accurate information about their daily location to facilitate **out-of-competition testing** without prior notice.
 
• **Therapeutic Use Exemptions (TUE):** Athletes may have illnesses or conditions that require them to take particular medications. If the medication falls under the **Prohibited List**, a **TUE** may give the athlete the authorization to take the needed medicine.
 
• **Sanctions:** Violations of anti-doping rules can lead to **disqualification** of results, **forfeiture** of medals, and **period of ineligibility** (bans) ranging from a few months to a lifetime.

4f

questions.question: According to the IMF World Economic Outlook, 2025, which of the following countries is projected to have the highest GDP growth among major economies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **IMF World Economic Outlook (WEO)** projections for **2025**, **India** is expected to remain the **fastest-growing major economy** in the world.
 
• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** has projected **India’s** GDP growth to be **6.5%** for the year **2025**, driven by strong **domestic demand** and a burgeoning **working-age population**. ***Hence, the correct option is India.***
 
• In comparison, **China's** economic growth is projected to slow down to approximately **4.1%** in **2025**, primarily due to the ongoing **property sector crisis** and subdued **consumer confidence**.
 
• The **United States of America** is projected to experience a growth rate of **1.9%**, reflecting a cooling labor market and the delayed effects of **monetary policy tightening**.
 
• **Japan** is expected to see a growth rate of about **1.1%**, as the economy continues to grapple with **demographic challenges** and modest **private consumption**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF):**
 
 
• It is a major financial agency of the **United Nations**, headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, and was established in **1944** during the **Bretton Woods Conference**.
 
• Currently, it consists of **190 member countries** working to foster global **monetary cooperation** and secure **financial stability**.
 
• The **World Economic Outlook (WEO)** is a comprehensive report published **twice a year** (April and October) that provides analysis and forecasts for the **global economy**.
 
 
 
• **GDP (Gross Domestic Product):**
 
 
• It is the **total market value** of all finished goods and services produced within a **country's borders** in a specific time period, serving as a scorecard of a country's **economic health**.
 
• India’s GDP surpassed the **$3.5 trillion** mark recently, making it the **fifth-largest economy** in the world by nominal GDP.
 
 
 
• **Global Growth Projections:**
 
 
• The **IMF** projects steady but slow **global growth** at approximately **3.2%** for **2025**, as central banks worldwide navigate **inflation** targets.
 
• Growth in **Emerging Market and Developing Economies (EMDEs)** continues to outpace **Advanced Economies**, with **Asia** remaining the main engine of **global expansion**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Growth Drivers for India:** Significant **public investment** in infrastructure, the **Production Linked Incentive (PLI)** scheme, and the **Digital India** initiative have been pivotal in maintaining high **growth trajectories**.
 
• **Monetary Policy:** The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** maintains an inflation target of **4%** (with a margin of +/- 2%), which helps in stabilizing the **macroeconomic environment** for sustained growth.
 
• **Key Figures:** **Kristalina Georgieva** serves as the **Managing Director** of the IMF, while **Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas** is the **Chief Economist** responsible for the **WEO** reports.
 
• **Fiscal Consolidation:** The Indian government aims to reduce the **fiscal deficit** to below **4.5%** of GDP by **2025-26**, which is a key factor monitored by **global rating agencies**.

questions.question: Which of the following measures did the Delhi government and IIT Kanpur attempt in October 2025 to clear smog that eventually proved unsuccessful due to low atmospheric moisture?

options.text: Deploying large-scale air purifiers in all public parks
Restricting industrial operations for one week

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cloud-seeding to induce artificial rain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **October 2025**, the **Delhi government** collaborated with researchers from **IIT Kanpur** to implement **cloud-seeding** as an emergency measure to mitigate the hazardous **smog** and **air pollution** levels in the city.
 
• The project aimed to induce **artificial rain** to facilitate the **washout effect**, which effectively removes suspended particulate matter like **PM2.5** and **PM10** from the atmosphere.
 
• The attempt eventually proved **unsuccessful** because the implementation of **cloud-seeding** requires specific meteorological conditions, including a minimum of **40% to 50% atmospheric moisture** and the presence of **rain-bearing clouds**.
 
• During the specified period in **October 2025**, the **humidity levels** were too low and the sky lacked the necessary **cumulus cloud** formations, rendering the chemical dispersal from aircraft ineffective. ***Hence, the correct answer is Cloud-seeding to induce artificial rain.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cloud Seeding Technology:**
 
 
• It is a **weather modification** technique where substances such as **silver iodide**, **potassium iodide**, or **dry ice** are dispersed into the air to serve as **cloud condensation nuclei**.
 
• In India, **IIT Kanpur** has developed a specialized **flaring attachment** for aircraft to carry out this process, which was previously tested in **2023**.
 
 
 
• **Delhi's Pollution Dynamics:**
 
 
• The **National Capital Region (NCR)** experiences a seasonal spike in **AQI (Air Quality Index)** during **October and November** due to **stubble burning** in Punjab and Haryana, combined with **firecracker emissions** and **calm wind conditions**.
 
• A phenomenon known as **temperature inversion** traps pollutants close to the ground, creating a thick layer of **smog** that poses severe health risks to the **30 million** residents of the region.
 
 
 
• **Other Mitigation Measures:**
 
 
• The **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)** is the primary regulatory framework used in Delhi, which involves **restricting construction**, **banning diesel generators**, and implementing the **odd-even vehicle scheme**.
 
• The government has also installed **smog towers** at **Connaught Place** and **Anand Vihar**, though their effectiveness is limited to a very small **radius of 1 km**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Constraints:** **Artificial rain** is not a permanent solution for **air pollution**; it is a temporary relief mechanism that is highly dependent on **unpredictable weather patterns** and **wind direction**.
 
• **Technical Collaboration:** The **Delhi government** offered to fund the entire cost of the **IIT Kanpur** project, estimated at several **crores of rupees**, provided the **Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)** and **Ministry of Defence** provided the necessary **airspace clearances**.
 
• **Health Impact:** Persistent **smog** in **2025** led to a **20% increase** in respiratory ailments among children and the elderly, necessitating the exploration of high-tech solutions like **cloud-seeding**.
</ul

questions.question: In November 2024, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) launched India’s inaugural analog space mission at __________ with an aim to simulate interplanetary habitat conditions and helping scientists explore the feasibility of establishing a sustainable base station beyond Earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2024**, the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** launched India’s **inaugural analog space mission** in **Leh**, **Ladakh**.
 
• The mission is a collaborative effort involving **ISRO’s Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC)**, **Aakaar Space**, the **University of Ladakh**, **IIT Bombay**, and the **Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC)**.
 
• The primary objective of this mission is to simulate **interplanetary habitat conditions**, providing a controlled environment to study the challenges of living on the **Moon** or **Mars**.
 
• The mission aims to explore the feasibility of establishing a **sustainable base station** beyond **Earth** by testing life support systems, resource management, and communication protocols.
 
• **Leh** was selected as the site for this mission because its **geographical** and **climatic features**—including high altitude, low oxygen levels, extreme cold, and barren landscape—closely mimic the **lunar and martian environments**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Analog Space Missions:**
 
 
• These are field tests conducted in locations on **Earth** that have physical similarities to extreme **space environments**.
 
• They are used to test **robotics**, **habitats**, **spacesuits**, and **human psychology** in isolation before actual spaceflight.
 
• International agencies like **NASA** and **ESA** conduct similar missions in locations like **Antarctica** and the **Atacama Desert**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Ladakh for Space Research:**
 
 
• Known as a **cold desert**, **Ladakh** offers unique **geological analogs** for **Mars**, specifically its volcanic rocks and permafrost.
 
• The **low atmospheric pressure** and **low humidity** in **Leh** provide an ideal setting to test the durability of **spacecraft materials**.
 
 
 
• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation):**
 
 
• Founded on **August 15, 1969**, and headquartered in **Bengaluru**.
 
• **ISRO** is currently working on the **Gaganyaan** mission, which is **India’s** first human spaceflight program.
 
• The organisation has also planned the **Bharatiya Antariksh Station** (Indian Space Station), targeted for completion by **2035**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU):** One of the mission's focuses is **ISRU**, which involves learning how to use local materials (like lunar regolith) to **construct structures** or produce **oxygen** and **water**.
 
• **Human Factors:** The mission tracks the **circadian rhythms**, **mental health**, and **physical health** of participants living in a confined **analog habitat**.
 
• **Future Prospects:** Successful data from the **Leh analog mission** will contribute to the design of the **habitat modules** for **India's** future missions to the **Moon** under the **Chandrayaan** program.

• **July 2025** marks a significant timeline for the completion of several **PMJVK** projects sanctioned during the previous fiscal years to ensure **last-mile delivery** of government services.

• The historic first-ever **Kho Kho World Cup** was hosted in **New Delhi**, India, from **13 to 19 January 2025**.
 
• The tournament took place at the iconic **Indira Gandhi Arena** (Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium), which is known for hosting major international sporting events.
 
• The event was jointly organized by the **Kho Kho Federation of India (KKFI)** and the **International Kho Kho Federation** to elevate the traditional Indian sport to a global platform.
 
• A total of **24 countries** from **six continents** participated in the competition, featuring **16 men's teams** and **16 women's teams** in their respective categories.
 
• The tournament aimed to promote the indigenous sport of **India** internationally, showcasing the speed, agility, and strategy inherent in **Kho Kho**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of Kho Kho:** 
 
 
• **Kho Kho** is one of the oldest traditional tag sports in **India**, with its modern origins traced back to the state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• Historically, it was played on 'raths' or chariots and was known as **Rathera**.
 
 
 
• **Kho Kho Federation of India (KKFI):** 
 
 
• The **KKFI** was established in the year **1955** to standardize the rules and promote the sport across the country.
 
• The current **President** of the **Kho Kho Federation of India** is **Sudhanshu Mittal**, who has been instrumental in organizing the inaugural World Cup.
 
 
 
• **International Kho Kho Federation:** 
 
 
• This body oversees the global development of the sport and works towards its inclusion in multi-sport events like the **Asian Games** and eventually the **Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Tournament Theme:** 
 
 
• The slogan for the **2025 World Cup** was "**Lakhon Dil, Ek Dhadkan**" (Millions of hearts, one heartbeat), emphasizing the emotional connection of the Indian populace with this native sport.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Support:** The **Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, under the **Government of India**, provided extensive support for the event as part of the initiative to promote indigenous games.
 
• **Technical Evolution:** The transition from playing on **mud surfaces** to **synthetic mats** has been a significant factor in making the sport more professional and visually appealing for international broadcasting.
 
• **Ultimate Kho Kho (UKK):** The success of the professional league, **Ultimate Kho Kho**, which launched its first season in **2022**, played a pivotal role in building the momentum and viewership required to host a **World Cup** in **2025**.
 
• **Global Reach:** Apart from **India**, nations like **England**, **South Africa**, **Nepal**, **Bhutan**, and **Malaysia** have emerged as strong contenders, indicating the growing popularity of the sport outside South Asia.
</ul

questions.question: Which veteran actor and dancer, noted for her appearances in films like ‘Navrang’ and ‘Pinjra’, passed away in October 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sandhya Shantaram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The veteran Indian actress and dancer **Sandhya Shantaram**, widely recognized for her prolific work in **Marathi** and **Hindi cinema**, passed away in **October 2025**.
 
• She was particularly celebrated for her lead roles in cinematic masterpieces directed by the legendary filmmaker **V. Shantaram**, such as the musical **Navrang (1959)** and the tragic drama **Pinjra (1972)**.
 
• Born as **Vijaya Deshmukh**, she was discovered by **V. Shantaram** and cast in the film **Amar Bhoopali** in **1951**, marking the beginning of a legendary career spanning several decades.
 
• She was known for her exceptional **classical dance** abilities, which were showcased extensively in films like **Jhalak** and **Do Aankhen Barah Haath (1957)**.
 
• Her performance in **Pinjra** is considered a milestone in **Marathi cinema**, where she played the role of a **Tamasha** dancer who challenges the moral fiber of a village teacher. ***Hence, the correct answer is Sandhya Shantaram.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significant Films:**
 
 
• **Navrang (1959):** This film is famous for its vibrant **Holi** sequences and the iconic song "**Tu Chhupi Hai Kahan**". **Sandhya** played a dual role (real-life wife and the protagonist's muse), showcasing her versatility as an actor and **kathak** dancer.
 
• **Pinjra (1972):** It was the first **Marathi film** to be produced in **color**. The film explored themes of morality, social fall, and the **Lavani** folk dance culture of **Maharashtra**.
 
• **Do Aankhen Barah Haath (1957):** In this socially relevant film about **prison reform**, she played the role of a toy seller, contributing to a project that won the **Silver Bear** at the **Berlin International Film Festival**.
 
 
 
• **Association with Rajkamal Kalamandir:**
 
 
• Most of her work was produced under the banner of **Rajkamal Kalamandir**, one of India's most prestigious film studios located in **Mumbai**.
 
• She married **V. Shantaram** in the **1950s** and remained a core part of his creative vision until his death in **1990**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy in Dance:**
 
 
• Unlike many actors of her era, **Sandhya** performed high-intensity **classical** and **folk dance** sequences without the use of body doubles, often undergoing rigorous training for months to perfect her movements for the **big screen**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **V. Shantaram:** A pioneer of **Indian Cinema**, he was a recipient of the **Dadasaheb Phalke Award** in **1985**. His films often focused on **social reform** and **humanism**.
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Jyoti Chandekar:** A well-known **Marathi stage** and film actress, known for her powerful character roles, but she is not the lead associated with **Navrang**.
 
• **Sulakshana Pandit:** An actress and **playback singer** prominent in the **1970s** and **1980s**, known for her roles in **Bollywood** but not primarily for **Shantaram's** early classics.
 
• **Madhumati:** A famous **dancer** and actress in **Hindi cinema** known for her **item numbers** and character roles during the **Golden Era** of the **1960s**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: With which of the following government bodies, did the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) collaborate in June 2025 to curb spam loan and credit‑card calls?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)** entered into a strategic collaboration to tackle the growing menace of **spam calls** and **SMS** related to **unsolicited loan offers** and **credit card** services.
 
• The primary objective of this partnership is to safeguard consumers from **financial fraud** and harassment caused by **unregistered telemarketers** who bypass standard regulatory protocols.
 
• As part of the initiative, the **RBI** issued directives to all **Scheduled Commercial Banks** and **NBFCs** to ensure that their third-party agents strictly adhere to **TRAI’s** guidelines regarding **Unsolicited Commercial Communications (UCC)**.
 
• The collaboration involves the implementation of **AI-driven filters** and **blockchain-based Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT)** to monitor and block **headers** and **templates** used by scammers to impersonate legitimate financial institutions.
 
• This move follows a significant rise in complaints regarding **digital lending apps** and **spam calls** that often lead to **phishing** attacks and unauthorized data harvesting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI):**
 
 
• Established on **February 20, 1997**, under the **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997**, to regulate telecom services in India.
 
• It is headquartered in **New Delhi** and functions as a **statutory body** to ensure transparency and healthy competition in the telecom sector.
 
• **TRAI** introduced the **Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations (TCCCPR)** in **2018** to provide a framework for controlling **spam** and protecting **subscriber privacy**.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• The **RBI** was established on **April 1, 1935**, in accordance with the provisions of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• As the **Central Bank** of the country, it regulates the **monetary policy** and oversees the **banking system** to maintain financial stability.
 
• In recent years, the **RBI** has introduced **Digital Lending Guidelines (2022)** to protect borrowers from **predatory lending practices** and **illegal loan apps**.
 
 
 
• **Unsolicited Commercial Communication (UCC):**
 
 
• This refers to any **commercial communication** that a subscriber receives without their **explicit consent**.
 
• The **DND (Do Not Disturb)** registry, managed by **TRAI**, allows users to opt-out of receiving such communications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Joint Working Group** formed by **RBI** and **TRAI** focuses on technical solutions like **Calling Name Presentation (CNAP)**, which helps users identify the **caller’s identity** before answering.
 
• The **Sanchar Saathi** portal, launched by the **Department of Telecommunications (DoT)**, also plays a crucial role in reporting **fraudulent mobile connections** and **spam**.
 
• Financial institutions found violating these norms face heavy **penalties** under the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, and **TRAI** regulations.
 
• This initiative is a critical step toward the **Digital India** vision, ensuring a **secure digital ecosystem** for **online banking** and **financial transactions**.

8f

questions.question: Who was named Sportsperson of the Year with a Disability at the 2025 Laureus Awards?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jiang Yuyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Jiang Yuyan**, a phenomenal **para-swimmer** from **China**, was officially named the **Sportsperson of the Year with a Disability** at the **2025 Laureus World Sports Awards**.

• The award recognizes her historic and dominant performance during the **Paris 2024 Paralympic Games**, where she emerged as the most successful athlete of the entire event.

• During the **Paris 2024** games, she won an incredible **seven gold medals**, competing in various individual and relay events within the **S6** and **S7** classifications.

• Her gold medal tally included victories in the **50m freestyle S6**, **100m freestyle S7**, **400m freestyle S6**, and **50m butterfly S6**, alongside multiple relay successes.

• At only **19 years old** at the time of the games, she became a symbol of excellence and resilience, breaking several **world records** and **Paralympic records** in the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Background of Jiang Yuyan:**

• Born in **2004** in **Shaoxing**, **Zhejiang province**, **China**, she faced significant adversity early in life after losing her right arm and right leg in a car accident at the age of **four**.

• She is widely known by the nickname **"Flying Fish"** due to her extraordinary speed and technique in the swimming pool.

• She began her international career with a breakthrough at the **2019 World Para Swimming Championships** in **London**, where she won **three gold medals** at the age of **14**.

• **The Laureus World Sports Awards:**

• Established in **1999**, these awards are often considered the "Oscars of Sport," honoring the greatest sporting achievements of the previous calendar year.

• The **Sportsperson of the Year with a Disability** category is one of the most prestigious honors in the **Paralympic** movement, highlighting athletes who overcome physical challenges to reach the pinnacle of sport.

• The winners are selected through a two-step process: a nominations panel of world media followed by a final vote by the **Laureus World Sports Academy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Paralympic Dominance:** **Jiang Yuyan’s** **seven gold medals** in a single **Paralympic Games** is a rare feat that places her among the all-time greats, comparable to legendary swimmers like **Michael Phelps** in the **Olympic** context.

• **Classification System:** In para-swimming, **S6** and **S7** refer to physical impairment classifications. The lower the number, the more severe the activity limitation. **Jiang's** ability to break records across multiple classes showcases her versatility.

• **Laureus Academy:** The final voting body for these awards, the **Laureus World Sports Academy**, consists of **71** of the greatest living sporting legends, ensuring that the winners are recognized by their peers.

• **China's Performance:** **Jiang's** contributions were pivotal in helping **China** top the medal table at the **Paris 2024 Paralympics** with a total of **94 gold medals** and **220 medals** overall.

questions.question: In March 2025, the government of which of the following states announced to bring 5,000 hectares under afforestation during the year 2025-2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government of **Himachal Pradesh**, during the presentation of its administrative goals in **March 2025**, announced a significant environmental target to bring **5,000 hectares** of land under **afforestation** during the financial year **2025-2026**.
 
• This initiative is part of the state's broader vision to enhance its **green cover** and mitigate the impacts of **climate change** in the fragile **Himalayan ecosystem**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the 5,000-hectare target is correct for Himachal Pradesh.***
 
• The **afforestation** drive will focus on the plantation of **broad-leaved trees** and species that are resilient to **forest fires**, which is a major concern for the state during the summer months.
 
• The **Himachal Pradesh Forest Department** has been designated as the nodal agency to identify degraded forest lands and community lands for this massive plantation exercise.
 
• The project also aims to involve **local communities** and **Panchayati Raj Institutions** to ensure the survival rate of the saplings and to promote **community-led conservation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical and Forest Profile:**
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh** has a total geographical area of **55,673 sq km**, out of which a significant portion is classified under recorded forest area.
 
• According to the **India State of Forest Report (ISFR)**, the state has been consistently working to increase its **forest cover** from the current levels to reach the national goal of **33%**.
 
• The state is home to diverse flora, including **Deodar (Cedrus deodara)**, **Oak**, **Kail**, and **Chir Pine**.
 
 
 
• **Green State Vision:**
 
 
• The **Government of Himachal Pradesh** has set an ambitious target to transform the state into a **"Green Energy State"** by **March 31, 2026**.
 
• The **afforestation** target of **5,000 hectares** for **2025-2026** complements this vision by creating **carbon sinks** to offset emissions.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• Forests in **Himachal Pradesh** play a crucial role in **watershed management**, providing water to several downstream states in **North India** through rivers like the **Beas**, **Ravi**, and **Sutlej**.
 
• **Eco-tourism** is a major source of revenue for the state, which is directly dependent on the preservation of its **natural landscapes** and **wildlife habitats**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Major Schemes:**
 
 
• The state implements various schemes like **"Ek Buta Beti Ke Naam,"** where saplings are planted to celebrate the birth of a girl child, linking **social forestry** with **gender empowerment**.
 
• The **"Mukhyamantri Van Vistaar Yojana"** is another key initiative focused on expanding **greenery** in barren and rocky terrains.
 
 
 
• **Climate Resilience:**
 
 
• The **2025-2026** plan emphasizes **soil moisture conservation** through the construction of **check dams** and **ponds** alongside afforestation to prevent **soil erosion** and **landslides**.
 
• The state has also been exploring **carbon credit** mechanisms to incentivize **sustainable forest management**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In January 2025, Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma inaugurated the 6th Meghalaya Games at which venue in Jowai?

__

• The prestigious multi-sporting event was hosted at the **Wahiajer Multi Sports Complex Stadium**, which is located in **Jowai** within the **West Jaintia Hills** district.

• **Meghalaya State Olympic Association (MSOA):**

• **Previous Editions:** 
 
 
• The **5th edition** of the Meghalaya Games was held in **January 2024** in **Tura**, West Garo Hills, and was inaugurated by the **President of India**, **Droupadi Murmu**.

questions.question: Dr. C Anandharamakrishnan received the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar 2024 in the Vigyan Shri category for his contribution to the field of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agricultural Science**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dr. **C Anandharamakrishnan** has been conferred with the prestigious **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar 2024** in the **Vigyan Shri** category for his pioneering work in **Agricultural Science**.
 
• He currently serves as the **Director** of the **CSIR-National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (NIIST)**, located in **Thiruvananthapuram**, **Kerala**.
 
• The **Vigyan Shri** award specifically recognizes individuals who have made distinguished contributions to any field of **science and technology**.
 
• His research expertise spans several critical areas, including **food engineering**, **3D food printing**, **nanotechnology** for food packaging, and **engineered digestive systems**.
 
• The **2024** awards ceremony was held on **August 23, 2024**, which coincided with the first-ever **National Space Day** in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (RVP):**
 
 
• This national award was instituted in **2023** by the **Government of India** to simplify and unify the diverse science awards previously given by various ministries.
 
• It is categorized into four levels: **Vigyan Ratna** (Lifetime Achievement), **Vigyan Shri** (Distinguished Contribution), **Vigyan Yuva-SSB** (Young Scientists), and **Vigyan Team**.
 
• The awards are open to persons of Indian origin (**PIO**) and **non-resident Indians (NRI)**, in addition to citizens of **India**.
 
 
 
• **Dr. C Anandharamakrishnan's Career:**
 
 
• Before his tenure at **CSIR-NIIST**, he served as the **Director** of the **National Institute of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM)**, **Thanjavur**.
 
• He holds a **Doctoral degree** from **Loughborough University**, **United Kingdom**, and has been instrumental in developing **spray drying** and **electrospraying** techniques for nutrient delivery.
 
• He is a Fellow of the **National Academy of Sciences (NASI)** and the **Royal Society of Chemistry**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 2024 Awards:**
 
 
• The **2024** edition marked the **inaugural** distribution of these unified national science awards.
 
• A total of **33 awards** were announced across various disciplines like **Physics**, **Chemistry**, **Biological Sciences**, and **Mathematics**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Award Selection:** The final recipients are selected by a high-level committee chaired by the **Principal Scientific Adviser** to the **Government of India**.
 
• **Date of Announcement:** The names of the awardees are officially announced on **May 11** every year, which is celebrated as **National Technology Day**.
 
• **National Space Day:** The **President of India**, **Droupadi Murmu**, presented the awards at **Rashtrapati Bhavan** on **August 23**, celebrating the anniversary of the **Chandrayaan-3** mission's success.
 
• **Scientific Impact:** In the field of **Agricultural Science**, Dr. Anandharamakrishnan’s work helps in addressing **food security** and improving the **shelf-life** of agricultural produce through advanced **bioprocessing**.
